title: Refactor decision fabric and failover choreography for smart routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Background: Over the last 18 months the smart routing layer accrued several incremental fixes: regional affinity hacks, synchronous fallback gating, and locks in the policy evaluator hotpath. These were pragmatic but now inhibit latency targets and make behavioral reasoning difficult. Goal: Replace ad-hoc routing logic with a smaller, well-documented 'decision fabric'—a composable evaluator pipeline plus a deterministic failover choreography that separates policy decisions from execution and makes fallbacks observable and testable.
problem_statement: Current router mixes policy evaluation, capacity checks, and failover side effects in a single hotpath. This causes intermittent 99th percentile latency spikes, race conditions during capacity flaps, and makes canary rollouts hard to reason about. Several downstream incidents traced to tangled state and region-specific fallthroughs.
proposal_summary: Introduce a thin Decision Fabric API that composes policy evaluators (latency SLO, cost preference, region affinity) and emits an immutable decision snapshot. Implement a separate Failover Choreographer which, given a decision snapshot and runtime signals (capacity, health, circuit-breakers), computes ordered fallback actions without mutating shared router state. Add tracing hooks and decision IDs to aid post-mortem and metrics correlation.
scope: In-scope: design and implement Decision Fabric interfaces; refactor existing policy predicates into evaluators; implement Failover Choreographer; migrate one regional route shard (us-east-1) as a pilot; add unit and integration tests; add telemetry for decision snapshots. Out-of-scope: UI changes, Dedicated autoscaler integration, full multi-region migration (follow-ups).
non_goals: Do not change model selection heuristics beyond refactoring. Do not address KV cache optimizations in this ticket. Do not modify customer-facing API surface.
migration_plan: 1) Add decision_fabric feature flag default-off. 2) Implement evaluators and choreographer behind flag. 3) Run pilot in us-east-1 with 10% traffic, mirror-decisions mode for 48h. 4) Collect metrics and compare decision divergence. 5) Ramp to 50% then 100% if divergence <1% and no latency regressions. 6) Gradually refactor other shards in follow-up tickets.
rollout_plan: Week 1: library + unit tests on feature flag. Week 2: pilot in us-east-1 (10% traffic, logging enabled). Week 3: analyze metrics and fix issues. Week 4: ramp to 50% then 100% if thresholds met. Gate: <5ms p99 router latency delta and no increase in fallback rate > 0.5%.
acceptance_criteria: Decision Fabric implements composable evaluator API and is documented in Confluence
Failover Choreographer produces deterministic ordered fallback lists and is covered by unit tests
Pilot in us-east-1 shows router latency p99 delta <5ms and fallback rate change <0.5%
All new code is behind feature flag and togglable per-region
Tracing includes decision_id and evaluator version for every routed request
Migration runbook and rollback steps documented and reviewed

notes: Trade-offs considered: (1) eagerly compute full decision snapshot vs lazy evaluation — chose eager snapshot for observability and deterministic failover ordering; (2) keep simple evaluator interface to lower migration cost at expense of duplicating small checks in multiple evaluators.
qa_plan: Unit tests for each evaluator, integration tests using traffic mirroring, chaos tests simulating capacity flaps, and synthetic load tests measuring p50/p95/p99 routing latency. Automated gating in CI for feature flag branches.
risk_mitigation: Feature-flagged rollout, pilot in single region, decision divergence alerts, automated rollback if p99 latency delta >5ms or fallback rate >0.5% increase.
estimated_impact: Medium — reduces router complexity and should lower p99 by removing locks and centralizing fallback logic; follow-up needed for full multi-region rollout.
